title: Three Running Shoes for New Runners in India (2026)
summary: Three men's road running shoes that differ in purpose: Nike Revolution 7, Nike Structure 26 and Skechers GO RUN Ride 11. Facts come from the makers' own pages.
description: Plain help for choosing a first running shoe in India. Three road shoes from Nike and Skechers, with notes on cushioning, drop, weight and fit.
lead: Which running shoe should a beginner look at in India? Here are three men's road running shoes that differ in purpose. The Nike Revolution 7 is listed by Nike for road running. Nike says the Structure 26 is best suited for runners who want a supportive daily trainer. The Skechers GO RUN Ride 11 is described by Skechers as a lightweight road running performance lace-up with a carbon fibre infused plate. Product facts come only from each maker's own page, and the two Nike pages we cite are Nike's UK pages. The buying tips come from Nike's fitting guide and Wikipedia. Nike's guide says beginners and experienced runners don't necessarily need different shoes, and adds: rather than choosing a shoe based on your experience level, choose one based on the types of runs you'll be doing. In our view, the Budget, Mid-range and Premium badges are only a rough grouping of these three shoes and are not stated by the makers. In our view, check that the exact model name matches before you order.

picks.name: Nike Revolution 7 (Men's)
picks.label: Nike lists it for road running
picks.verdict: Nike's UK page lists it as a men's road running shoe. It says the foam midsole delivers a soft, smooth ride.
paragraphs: Nike's UK page lists the Revolution 7 as a men's road running shoe with a heel-to-toe drop of 10 mm. It says a foam midsole delivers a soft, smooth ride. The product details give the weight as approx. 286 g for men's UK size 9, while the tech specs say approx. 282.8 g for men's size 9.

Nike's UK page says a generative traction pattern and rubber lugs give extra grip on hills. It says the MR-10 last offers a little extra room in the forefoot and toe for comfort, and that there is more room in the forefoot compared with the Revolution 6, so your toes don't feel pinched.

Nike's UK page says the MR-10 last offers a little extra room in the forefoot and toe for comfort.

not_good: Nike's UK page lists two slightly different weights: approx. 286 g (men's UK 9) in the product details and approx. 282.8 g (men's size 9) in the tech specs.

picks.name: Nike Structure 26 (Men's)
picks.label: Nike: best suited to runners wanting a supportive daily trainer
picks.verdict: Nike's UK page lists it as a men's road running shoe and says it is best suited for runners who want a supportive daily trainer. It says the shoe fits small and recommends ordering half a size up, though the page's FAQ also says most runners should start with their usual size.
paragraphs: Nike's UK page lists the Structure 26 as a men's road running shoe with a heel-to-toe drop of 10 mm. It says the full-length ReactX midsole delivers a cushioned yet stable transition from heel to toe-off. The page also mentions a higher stack height for stability and support. The product details give the weight as approx. 321 g for men's size 9, and the tech specs say approx. 320 g.

Nike's UK page says its midfoot support system helps to slow the rate of ankle eversion and provides a stable platform. It says the plush collar and tongue, along with the engineered mesh upper, provide comfort, support and an improved fit. The page says the shoe fits small and recommends ordering half a size up, while its FAQ says most runners should start with their usual size. The FAQ also says the shoe is best suited for runners who want a supportive daily trainer.
good: Nike's UK page says the midfoot support system helps to slow the rate of ankle eversion and provides a stable platform.
Nike's UK page says the full-length ReactX midsole delivers a cushioned yet stable transition from heel to toe-off.
Nike's UK page says the shoe has reflective design details.
not_good: Nike's UK page says the shoe fits small and recommends ordering half a size up, though its FAQ also says most runners should start with their usual size. The two statements differ.
At approx. 321 g it is the heaviest of the three weights given in this guide, though each page labels its size slightly differently.

Wikipedia says most evidence-based comparisons show no reduction in lower-limb running injuries from prescribing different types of shoe for different foot types. In our view, that is a reason to try the shoe on for comfort and not to buy support on its own.

picks.name: Skechers GO RUN Ride 11 (Men's)
picks.label: Skechers lists a carbon fibre infused plate
cells: HYPER BURST ICE cushioning (dual-density HYPER BURST technology); carbon fiber infused plate
picks.verdict: Skechers describes it as a lightweight road running performance lace-up. The page gives a 6 mm offset, a 281 g weight and a 32 mm to 38 mm stack height.
paragraphs: Skechers India's page lists the GO RUN Ride 11 under men's and describes it as a lightweight road running performance lace-up with a breathable engineered mesh and synthetic upper. It says HYPER BURST ICE features dual-density HYPER BURST technology for a soft and stable run, and that a carbon fiber infused plate puts more spring in your step. The page gives a stack height of 32 mm to 38 mm, an offset of 6 mm and a weight of 9.9 oz / 281 g (men's 9).

The page lists a removable Skechers Arch Fit insole and, among its key features, podiatrist-certified arch support. It also lists a Goodyear Performance Outsole that it says delivers enhanced traction, stability and durability. It says the shoe is machine washable and lists US sizes 7 to 14. The page does not describe the fit or the width.

choose.heading: Nike on fit
choose.text: Nike's fitting guide says running shoes should fit true to size with approximately a thumb's width between your big toe and the end of the shoe. It says to size up if your toes feel cramped or press against the front of the shoe. It also says too-tight shoes can lead to lost or black toenails.

choose.heading: Nike on trying shoes on later in the day
choose.text: Nike's guide says feet tend to widen throughout the day, and it cites the National Institutes of Health for this. It says to shop in the afternoon or evening.

choose.heading: Nike on socks and orthotics
choose.text: Nike's guide says to wear your running socks and bring your orthotics.

choose.heading: Road and trail shoes
choose.text: Nike's guide says trail running shoes have sticky rubber outsoles or deep lugs for improved traction. Nike's UK pages list the Revolution 7 and the Structure 26 as road running shoes, and Skechers India's page describes the GO RUN Ride 11 as a road running performance lace-up.

choose.heading: Neutral or supportive
choose.text: Wikipedia says the majority of running shoes are for heel-toe joggers/runners, which are further subdivided into 'neutral', 'overpronation' and 'underpronation'. It also says most evidence-based comparisons show no reduction in lower-limb running injuries from prescribing different types of shoe for different foot types. Nike's page says the Structure 26 is best suited for runners who want a supportive daily trainer.

choose.heading: Nike on replacing shoes
choose.text: Nike's guide says a general guideline is to replace running shoes every 300 to 500 miles.

choose.heading: Check the model, width and size
choose.text: In our view, check that the page shows the exact model name, your size and the width you need before you order. Nike's page says the Structure 26 fits small, though its FAQ also says most runners should start with their usual size. Skechers India's page for the GO RUN Ride 11 lists US sizes 7 to 14 without describing the fit.

faq.q: Which of these should I pick?
faq.a: We do not rank these three, because they differ in purpose. Nike's UK page lists the Revolution 7 as a men's road running shoe with a foam midsole. Nike's page says the Structure 26 is best suited for runners who want a supportive daily trainer. Skechers describes the GO RUN Ride 11 as a lightweight road running performance lace-up with a carbon fibre infused plate.

faq.q: Do I need a stability shoe?
faq.a: Nike's guide says beginners and experienced runners don't necessarily need different shoes, and that rather than choosing a shoe based on your experience level, you should choose one based on the types of runs you'll be doing. Wikipedia says most evidence-based comparisons show no reduction in lower-limb running injuries from prescribing different types of shoe for different foot types. It also says the majority of running shoes are for heel-toe joggers/runners, which are further subdivided into 'neutral', 'overpronation' and 'underpronation'.

faq.q: What drop and weight do the makers list?
faq.a: Nike's UK pages list a heel-to-toe drop of 10 mm for both the Revolution 7 and the Structure 26. Nike lists the Revolution 7 at approx. 286 g (men's UK 9) and the Structure 26 at approx. 321 g (men's size 9). Skechers India's page lists the GO RUN Ride 11 with a 6 mm offset and a weight of 281 g (men's 9). In our view, the weights are only rough guides because the pages label their sizes differently.

faq.q: How much room should I leave at the toe?
faq.a: Nike's guide says approximately a thumb's width between your big toe and the end of the shoe. It also says to wear your running socks and bring your orthotics, and that feet tend to widen throughout the day.

faq.q: How often should running shoes be replaced?
faq.a: Nike's guide says a general guideline is every 300 to 500 miles.
